items.title: "She has given us a sense of security": the humanitarian midwives deployed to Blue Nile State
items.summary: Fighting in Blue Nile displaced tens of thousands of people this year, most of them women and children. UNFPA deployed 15 rapidly trained midwives to the camps; in their first three weeks they supported 140 safe deliveries and followed up more than 700 pregnant women.
items.quote: We provided emergency assistance and whatever support was needed.
items.quoteBy: Sa'aida, midwife, Al Karama 3 camp, Ad-Damazin

items.title: Surviving violence, rebuilding communities
items.summary: Ikhlas Awad Yaseen, a peacebuilder from Kordofan, led the Young Dream Charity Organization, a women-led group working on protection, education, peacebuilding and health for women and children affected by the war, with support from the Women's Peace and Humanitarian Fund.
items.quote: We have the power to rebuild our country.

items.title: Strength in solidarity: how mutual aid is helping women survive Sudan's war
items.place: Sennar, Gedaref, Kassala, Darfur and Khartoum
items.summary: Women's emergency response rooms provide sanitary products, medical and psychological support for survivors of sexual violence, and help for displaced women, often under threat and with little funding.
items.quote: To make life easier for women, surviving the war requires collective work and strength in solidarity.

items.title: Sudanese women farmers are hardest hit by the collapse of the food system
items.place: East Darfur, South Darfur and South Kordofan
items.summary: Women now carry most of the farming work. Of 492 farmers surveyed, 87% were women; 89% reported lower harvests and 56% could not harvest safely. CARE asks donors to fund women's farming groups directly.
